Because the legacy write now runs in a detached goroutine, the tests return before (or regardless of whether) d.Legacy.* is invoked; the mocks' legacy expectations are set up but never asserted with m.AssertCalled / AssertExpectations, and there is no synchronization (e.g. waiting on a channel or Eventually) to observe the async call. Consequently the tests cannot detect the critical regression where the legacy write never executes (e.g. due to the request-context cancellation bug in dualwriter_mode3.go): they would still pass. findings.body: The new 'with dual write (file, mode 3)' and 'with dual write (unified storage, mode 3)' subtests (lines 132-144 and 191-204) run the shared doPlaylistTests helper, which performs CRUD via the k8s API and then immediately reads via the legacy /api/playlists endpoints (e.g. getFromBothAPIs at line 610, and the legacy search at line 523).
